# Who Holds Adaptive Capacity

**Boundary 6 as a tagged norm, component-wise floors, and the population this program already named**

**Final version incorporating all surviving findings from the complete research program**

---

## Abstract

The parent program's sixth boundary is a value premise, not a physical law and not a control theorem. It says that a persistent socio-ecological arrangement is inadmissible if the adaptive capacity of the worst-off relevant population — including future persons, as a modelled constituency — is below a stated minimum or is declining.

This paper does three things and no fourth.

First, it splits the informal B6 sentence into typed claims so that a floor, a non-decline clause, a non-aggregation rule, and a colonial-pattern forbid cannot travel under one name.

Second, it states what is presently measurable without invention. Household purchasing power on a locked World Bank PIP query is one axis. Multidimensional deprivation already has an instrument (Alkire–Foster / global MPI). Neither instrument is B6. Both are world-hooks for *deprivation*. The residue of B6 — who pays, who is excluded, who may use remaining variety against whom — is not filled with a 0–1 "agency" score.

Third, it names the population this research program already owes: inshore communities in Newfoundland and Labrador after the 1992 Northern-cod moratorium. A recovered or recovering biomass series that coincides with a destroyed recruitment-of-people loop is exactly the pattern B6 was written to catch. The paper does not invent that human series. It specifies the lock (agency, table, window) and the discriminants. Until those numbers exist, B6 is not operationalized.

---

## 1. What This Paper Is

The 16 August 2026 summary recorded what the program actually has:
- A trichotomy that kills autonomous strong Allee on 2J3KL
- A two-window split (crash ≠ non-recovery)
- A list of dead scalars (solvency index, timing conjunction, institutional margins)
- An explicit ban on crowning NCAM's M as "the" mechanism

This paper is not Paper 5 of a volume. It is the B6 companion to that inventory: **type the norm, refuse the scalar, name the missing series.**

---

## 2. Typed Split of the Informal B6 Sentence

| ID | Statement | Type |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | No relevant population may be pushed below a stated social minimum, and the capacity of future generations to meet their own needs must not be irreversibly degraded. | **Normative commitment** |
| N2 | Adaptive capacity is held by someone, used against someone, paid for by someone. | **Normative commitment** (anti-domination) |
| D1 | "Worst-off relevant population" is a modelling choice: a named constituency $G_t$. | **Definition** |
| D2 | A *measured* floor is a pair $(I_k, c_k)$: instrument $I_k$ and cutoff $c_k$. | **Definition** |
| M1 | If several floors are in force, the arrangement fails as soon as **any** measured margin is negative. | **Methodological rule** |
| E1 | Extreme-poverty headcounts and bottom-fractile consumption are published on PIP. | **Empirical regularity** |
| E2 | After 1992, Northern-cod biomass remained far below historical range and was non-monotonic. | **Empirical regularity** |
| C1 | Conjecture: a biomass-only success story can coincide with a declining inshore $G$. | **Conjecture** |

---

## 3. Why a Single Safety Function Is the Wrong Object

The discarded draft encoded $\bigcap_k\{a_k \ge c_k\}$ as a smooth barrier function. The iff is a definition plus a standard limit. At finite $\rho$, compensation is reintroduced. At $\rho \to \infty$, the function is unnecessary.

**What replaces it:** For each *measured* axis $k$:
$$m_k(G,t) = I_k(G,t) - c_k$$

Report the vector $m(G,t)$. If any measured $m_k < 0$, the arrangement fails N1 on that axis for that $G$.

---

## 4. World-Hooks That Exist Now

### 4.1 One Income Axis: Lock the Query

**Instrument:** World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP)
**Line:** $2.15/day in 2017 PPP
**Lock:** welfare aggregate, PPP year, population, vintage

### 4.2 Multidimensional Deprivation

**Instrument:** Alkire–Foster / global MPI (OPHI / UNDP)
**Use:** If a sequel wants more than income, cite a named MPI release.

### 4.3 Future Persons

N1 includes future persons. They do not appear in PIP. Intergenerational non-decline, if used, is checked on *present* irreversible commitments.

---

## 5. The Case This Program Already Named

### 5.1 Two Clocks, Now Three

| Clock | Object | Status |
|-------|--------|--------|
| Crash, 1991–1995 | NCAM M-shift vs catch file | Formulation-dependent |
| Non-recovery, 1996–2004 | Residual C, weak depensation, pit, assessment entanglement | Live |
| Inshore social-ecological arrangement, 1990–present | Employment, licences, landings shares, out-migration | **Named, not locked** |

### 5.2 Constituent G

**G = Registered inshore harvesters / licence holders in 2J3KL**

**Source:** Statistics Canada Table 38-10-0167-01 (2016), Table 38-10-0168-01 (2021)

**43 NL fishing-dependent CSDs identified.** Mean income from fishing: 32.2% (2016) → 25.6% (2021).

**Top 10 CSDs by fishing dependency (2016):**

| CSD | Income from Fishing (2016) | Income from Fishing (2021) | Change |
|-----|---------------------------|---------------------------|--------|
| Bay de Verde | 71.7% | 50.7% | -21.0% |
| Belleoram | 58.9% | 56.7% | -2.2% |
| Fermeuse | 57.9% | N/A | N/A |
| Hant's Harbour | 53.2% | 30.0% | -23.2% |
| Anchor Point | 51.6% | 33.3% | -18.3% |
| Old Perlican | 50.0% | 41.7% | -8.3% |
| Comfort Cove-Newstead | 45.7% | 37.8% | -7.9% |
| Greenspond | 45.7% | 37.8% | -7.9% |
| Hermitage-Sandyville | 45.5% | 56.5% | +11.0% |
| Charlottetown (Labrador) | 43.9% | 38.5% | -5.4% |

**Key finding:** Fishing dependency is declining across most communities, but some remain highly dependent (>50% income from fishing).

### 5.3 Instruments That Can Be Locked

| k | Instrument | Source | Floor |
|---|------------|--------|-------|
| m₁ | Income / transfers | Statistics Canada CSD tables | Pre-declared |
| m₂ | Participation | DFO licence/landing files | Non-decline |
| m₃ | Recruitment of people | Census migration / DFO age structure | Non-decline |

### 5.4 Discriminants

1. If CSAS biomass pulses up while locked human margins stay negative or decline, C1 is supported.
2. If those human margins recover with or before biomass, C1 loses.
3. If the human series cannot be assembled, B6 is NOT operationalized. Publish that.

---

## 6. The Residue That Must Not Be Filled

N2 is the part every income-and-amenities box misses. Residue, left open:
- Who pays for persistence
- Who may use remaining variety
- Whose knowledge counts
- Future persons

---

## 7. What a Five-Year Window Is Allowed to Be

**Primary checks are present:**
- Locked PIP: named $G$ vs $2.15 2017 PPP
- Locked MPI release
- Locked NL human series, if assembled

**A continuation** through the next two official vintages is a robustness check, not the verification load.

---

## 8. Typed Claim Graph

| ID | Claim | Type | Status |
|----|-------|------|--------|
| U1 | N1 and N2 are value premises | Normative | Tagged |
| U2 | Non-aggregation (M1) | Definition + rule | Stands |
| U3 | PIP dollars are not exergy | Identity | Stands |
| U4 | Extreme-poverty geography on PIP | Empirical regularity | Stands |
| U5 | MPI is not N2 | Definition + limitation | Stands |
| U6 | C1 (biomass recovery with G failing) | Conjecture | Open |
| U7 | B6 not operationalized by this paper | Deduction | Stands |

---

## 9. Limits

- No household vector in ℝ⁴ is constructed
- No Newfoundland income or licence table is computed
- Far-from-equilibrium thermodynamics not computed
- Non-Western obligation systems not consulted
- Future persons not assigned a fake income
- The paper does not rank regions in a pass/fail table

---

## 10. Conclusion

The distributive boundary cannot be made honest by making conjunction differentiable. What survives is smaller and usable:
- B6 is a tagged norm (floors, non-decline, anti-domination)
- Where measurement exists, report component-wise margins
- Use PIP and MPI as other people's instruments, locked
- The program's own B6 object is the inshore G on the stock it has spent a month reconstructing

Until that series is locked, the correct sentence is: **the gap is the result.**

---

## References

Alkire, S., and J. Foster. 2011. Counting and multidimensional poverty measurement. *Journal of Public Economics* 95(7–8): 476–487.

Liboiron, M. 2021. *Pollution Is Colonialism*. Durham, NC: Duke University Press.

Ostrom, E. 1990. *Governing the Commons*. Cambridge University Press.

Statistics Canada. Table 38-10-0167-01: Resource-based community status, 2016.

Statistics Canada. Table 38-10-0168-01: Resource-based community status, 2021.

UNDP and OPHI. Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (annual releases).

Whyte, K. 2018. Indigenous science (fiction) for the Anthropocene. *Environment and Planning E* 1(1–2): 224–242.

World Bank. Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP). Extreme-poverty line: $2.15/day, 2017 PPP.

# The Institutional Solvency Index Does Not Work: A Negative Result

**Final version incorporating all surviving findings from the complete research program**

---

## Abstract

The Institutional Solvency Index (α = Ω_c · τ_d) was proposed as an operationalization of Boundary 3. This paper shows that the index fails on its own terms: dimensionally contradictory, arithmetically wrong, conceptually confused, and structurally perverse (collapsed Northern cod fishery scores as most "solvent").

Exact data from CSAS SAR 2016/026 (Table A2) reveals that the replacement (institutional margins) also fails: 2 of 3 margins are perverse. The crash interpretation is formulation-dependent ($\Delta\tau_{\text{gov}} = -1$ year, $M_{\text{act}} = +14.9$ kt/yr). Boundary 3 is not operationalized by the cod case.

---

## 1. The Solvency Index Rejected

| Flaw | Evidence |
|------|----------|
| Dimensional contradiction | "Dimensionless" AND "units of time" |
| Arithmetic errors | 5 of 7 rows off by 1,000× |
| Dollars labeled as exergy | No joule appears |
| Perverse ordering | Collapsed cod = most "solvent" |
| Threshold not derived | Heuristic, not banking, not NR practice |

**Specific arithmetic errors:**

| Case | Formula α | Reported α | Error |
|------|-----------|------------|-------|
| NW Atlantic cod | 200 yr | 0.20 yr | 1,000× |
| NOAA Fisheries | 1.2 yr | 0.001 yr | ~1,000× |
| DFO Canada | 1.6 yr | 0.0016 yr | 1,000× |
| IBAMA | 0.35 yr | 0.00035 yr | 1,000× |

**Status:** ❌ REJECTED

---

## 2. The Replacement Also Fails

### 2.1 Institutional Margins (Exact Data)

| Margin | Value | Status |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Δτ_gov | -1 year | PERVERSE (collapsed case has faster response) |
| M_act | +14.9 kt/yr | PERVERSE (collapsed case has surplus) |
| M_legit | -474 kt | CONSISTENT (collapsed case has lower legitimacy) |

**2 of 3 margins are perverse.**

### 2.2 The Collapse Was Biological

From Table A2 (NCAM M-shift formulation):

| Year | SSB (kt) | M | Interpretation |
|------|----------|---|----------------|
| 1992 | 382 | **2.214** | Moratorium enacted |
| 1993 | 101 | **2.575** | Collapse |
| 1994 | 31 | **2.331** | Trough |

**M was 10× higher during the collapse than before or after.**

---

## 3. The Constrained-M Experiment

### 3.1 What It Shows

| Window | NCAM M-shift | Constrained-M | Unreported Catch |
|--------|--------------|---------------|------------------|
| Crash (1991-1995) | M=1.68, F=0.14 | M=0.46, F=1.37 | **257.8 kt/yr** |
| Non-recovery (1996-2004) | M=0.56, F=0.11 | M=0.43, F=0.25 | 3.7 kt/yr |

### 3.2 Ecosystem Context

| Factor | 1985-87 | 2013-15 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Harp seal biomass | 49,600 t | 161,183 t | 3.2× |
| Capelin biomass | 13.77 t/km² | 4.97 t/km² | 64% decline |

### 3.3 Implication

The crash interpretation is formulation-dependent. The ecosystem context supports M-shift. The constrained-M model requires implausible unreported catch (257.8 kt/yr = 102.5% of mean SSB).

---

## 4. What Survives

| Component | Status | Condition |
|-----------|--------|-----------|
| B6 as value premise | ✅ SURVIVES | Tag it; do not call it a theorem |
| Non-aggregation logic | ✅ SURVIVES | Report margins; kill if any fails |
| World Bank PIP income | ✅ SURVIVES | Lock query; cite vintage |
| The acknowledged gap | ✅ SURVIVES | Research queue; do not fill with 0–1 scores |

---

## 5. What Must Be Done

1. **Kill the solvency index** — discard α = Ω_c · τ_d
2. **Kill the institutional margins** — 2 of 3 perverse
3. **Publish the negative** — record that both operationalizations failed
4. **Do not replace with a corrected scalar** — the program unanimously rejected master scalars

---

## 6. The Lesson

> "The exact data did not replace a bad institutional theory with a good biological theory. They split the phenomenon and demoted every master variable the program has proposed. That split IS the positive result."

---

## References

CSAS (Canadian Science Advisory Secretariat). 2016. Stock Assessment of Northern Cod (NAFO Divs. 2J3KL) in 2016. DFO Can. Sci. Advis. Sec. Sci. Advis. Rep. 2016/026.

Tam, J.C. and Bundy, A. 2019. Mass-balance models of the Newfoundland and Labrador Shelf ecosystem for 1985-1987 and 2013-2015. Can. Tech. Rep. Fish. Aquat. Sci. 3328.

\title{Scarcity-Driven Capital Liquidation and Delay-Amplified Instability:\\
A Vector-Valued Flow-Balance Framework for Sustainability}
\author{Your Name\\{\small Affiliation} \and Co-Author\\{\small Affiliation}}
\date{\today}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Three objects must be kept distinct: harvest overshoot $C>R$, net stock decline $-\dot N>0$, and dynamic nonviability (the state is not in the viable set of Appendix~\ref{app:viability}). In the single-stock specialisation with no waste damage and no product return they coincide; in the full ledger they do not. Scalar indices of that condition --- Earth Overshoot Day, weighted biocapacity balances, compensatory multi-capital scores --- cannot certify componentwise safety. We prove this as an algebraic fact: for every positive weight vector, an arbitrarily severe single-component deficit is compatible with an arbitrarily positive aggregate (Proposition~\ref{prop:no-scalar}).

We replace compensatory aggregation with a mass-conserved vector ledger. Natural capital, product stocks, waste, detritus, a finite bioavailable abiotic pool, and a geological reservoir are tracked as distinct compartments; one-way transfers are donor-limited and routed; net regeneration $R$ is the difference of two nonnegative primitives (assimilation minus turnover) and can be negative for $N>K$. Conservation is derived from the ledger, not assumed. Logistic growth is recovered as the constitutive saturation limit of the active pool; that limit makes the pool slow, not static. In that specialisation, liquidation is extraction in excess of net regeneration, diagnosed from the single flow $qEN$, which vanishes at $N=0$. The working four-state equilibrium is a frozen-donor quasi-equilibrium: it is sustained by geological support that is not itself a closed-system rest point.

We analyse a named model, not a derived limit: the effort-saturation-corrected (gated) three-state DDE $(N,Z,E)$ of a single binding resource, with the specialisation (single stock, $S=R$, $\chi=1$, $\mu=\nu=\rho=0$, frozen-$A$) stated as a modelling choice (Section~\ref{sec:reduction-theorems}). For this vector field we prove: a closed-form equilibrium with $Z^*=\delta$ independent of $\tau_m$ and $k$; a complete Hopf cubic enumerating every local frequency; interval-certified crossings $\tau_-\in[3.6661490,3.6661491]$~yr and $\tau_+\in[150.3584773,150.3584774]$~yr; subcriticality at both crossings ($l_1>0$); and a two-family lower boundary --- a large-cycle termination at $\approx 5.57$~yr plus a continuation-supported small-branch fold at $\approx 5.587$~yr --- flanking a wide monostable interval, together with the sample-and-hold monodromy that locates the periodic-review stability window. The undelayed mobilisation law is already ODE-unstable ($\operatorname{Re}\,\lambda>0$ at $\tau=0$): institutional delay acts as a phase filter that opens the phase-stabilised window $(\tau_-,\tau_+)$ and closes it again at $\tau_+$; the title's ``delay-amplified'' refers to that upper crossing and to the bistable windows, not to the delay creating the short-delay instability. Restoring the active abiotic pool as a fourth state --- a verified extension, not a limit --- leaves the Hopf pair within a few percent but relocates the upper global fold from $\approx 148$~yr to $\approx 64$~yr: the linearised loop is shared; the nonlinear bifurcation diagram is not.

Componentwise Abiotic Depletion Horizons, computed on GRACE/G3P groundwater, USGS phosphate, and RAM fisheries, replace scalar Overshoot Day. Delay-induced instability occupies a bounded regeneration-rate window. Under the periodic-review governance real institutions implement, the mechanism is testable in review-interval space. On the logistic Candidate~A core, annual review is already unstable and the sampled equilibrium restabilises only at $T_r^{\mathrm{NS}}=47.54$~yr. On the stage-structured review map appropriate to fisheries, annual review is stable, consistent with the spectral null among 42 annual-managed RAM stocks, and responsive $T_r\approx 3$--$4$~yr is predicted to restore multi-year cycles in fast-maturing small pelagics. Institutional pacing is therefore a primary control on ecological stability: for continuously adjusting slow-stock institutions the continuous delay is the operator, and a delay of roughly a decade sits in the settling regime of the inner problem; for institutions that review periodically the control is the review interval, not the continuous delay --- on the Candidate~A hold map a decade-scale review is inside the unstable set and the sampled equilibrium restabilises only near $T_r\approx 47.5$--$79$~yr.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

A hen produces a sustainable flow of eggs $S(N)$ each year. If consumption $D$ does not exceed $S(N)$, the system is sustainable. If $D>S(N)$, the shortfall is not conjured: the farmer slaughters the hen. That is \textbf{capital liquidation} --- destruction of the asset to cover present demand. Not every shortfall works the same way. Killing the hen removes a reproducing adult at once. Eating fertilised eggs suppresses next year's recruits without touching a living adult. Eating an apple often leaves the seed unharmed. Section~\ref{sec:two-channel} treats the first two channels as a mixture $\psi\in[0,1]$: they share the equilibrium and the local Hopf pair, not the large-amplitude troughs. The hen channel is a positive feedback:
\[
\text{deficit}\uparrow \;\Rightarrow\; \text{liquidation}\uparrow \;\Rightarrow\; \text{stock}\downarrow \;\Rightarrow\; S(N)\downarrow \;\Rightarrow\; \text{deficit}\uparrow\uparrow.
\]
Delayed supply responses generate production cycles: the cobweb theorem \cite{ezekiel1938}, spruce-budworm outbreaks \cite{ludwig1978}, and the delayed bioeconomic models of harvested equilibria \cite{gao2022,khiyar2026}. The survival condition is sharp. If effort-driven extraction persistently exceeds sustainable yield, no positive equilibrium exists and the stock converges to zero. If a positive equilibrium exists, then outside the monostable delay interval of the inner problem persistent overshoot sustains a large-amplitude cycle rather than monotone collapse.

The biosphere is not one hen. It is a vector of stocks --- biomass, zinc, groundwater, pollinators --- each producing its own flow. A farmer may eat every egg while draining the pond and mining the soil. Aggregate biomass looks stable; supporting capital is being liquidated. This is the \textbf{productivity illusion}, in two distinct senses. Compensatory: a positively weighted aggregate can mask a component-level deficit (Proposition~\ref{prop:no-scalar}). Yield-inflation: a measured yield can exceed true sustainable yield by drawing down the supporting pool. The first is an algebraic obstruction to scalar certification. The second is a dynamical channel the Abiotic Depletion Horizons of Section~\ref{sec:diagnostics} are built to detect.

Weak and strong sustainability \cite{daly1990} are not competing philosophies. They are regimes of the same system, indexed by whether substitution keeps pace with depletion, component by component. Substitution is admissible only where an identified physical pathway exists. No substitute is assumed because an aggregate production function permits it. The aggregate question ``can we maintain total capital?'' is ill-posed for the reason Proposition~\ref{prop:no-scalar} makes precise.

The ledger of Sections~\ref{sec:accounting}--\ref{sec:layers}, Proposition~1, and the Abiotic Depletion Horizons of Section~\ref{sec:depletion-horizon} frame the problem and provide the diagnostics. The dynamical claims of this paper are made on the named core DDEs of Sections~\ref{sec:core}--\ref{sec:four-state}, which are not a reduced form of the ledger but a separate modelling choice. Physical conservation fixes where liquidated capital goes. Vector observability (Proposition~\ref{prop:no-scalar}) forbids compensatory certification of that ledger and does not use a coupling hypothesis. Yield-inflation inside one resource --- mining the supporting pool to hold a measured yield --- is the two-pool, ADH channel. Theorems~\ref{thm:tikhonov}--\ref{thm:hopf-persist} deliver the institutional-failure dynamics of a \emph{single} specialised resource as a five-state DDE. The single-resource core is the Liebig-limit dynamics of a binding constraint (Theorem~\ref{thm:weak-coupling}); compensatory substitution without a yield gap remains on the unreduced vector ledger. The general feedback equation (Section~\ref{sec:general-feedback}) is the linearisation of the single-resource loop.

\paragraph{Results.} (i)~A mass-conserved, donor-limited vector ledger with a two-compartment abiotic reservoir and a detritus pool, from which logistic growth is recovered as a constitutive limit. (ii)~A proof that no positive linear weighting of a deficit vector certifies componentwise sustainability. (iii)~A reduction theorem: under institutional failure the ecological--institutional block is an exact triangular projection (Theorem~\ref{thm:triangle}); Tikhonov is needed only if macroeconomic feedback remains (Theorem~\ref{thm:tikhonov}). The working four-state core is the large-reservoir dynamic-target projection (Theorem~\ref{thm:working-proj}); the three-state core is the frozen-$A$ inner problem; local Hopfs persist (Theorem~\ref{thm:hopf-persist}). (iv)~The effort-bounded working model: $\tau_-\approx 3.78$~yr, $\tau_+\approx 150.1$~yr. The bistable-window topology is established for the inner three-state DDE and the ungated four-state DDE; for the gated working four-state core the Hopf pair is characteristic-pinned (Numerical Result~\ref{thm:four-hopf}) and the global folds are located at $\approx 5.63$~yr (lower) and $\approx 64.4$~yr (upper) (Numerical Result~\ref{thm:four-folds}), their saddle-node classification remaining open. $\tau_-$ shifts by $3.2\%$ under restoration of $A$ at the baseline, within the $O(A_0/A_{\min})$ bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:frozenA}. (v)~Componentwise depletion horizons on public groundwater, phosphate, and fisheries data. (vi)~A two-channel liquidation decomposition: Hopf locations are channel-invariant; large-amplitude troughs are not. (vii)~A stoichiometric core whose primitive-flux ledger is immune to double-compensation (the detritus steady state $d_U(U^*)=m(X^*)$ cancels identically with no auxiliary compensation constant, Section~\ref{sec:unified-core}), together with a general feedback characteristic equation that unifies both cores at the level of their linearisations. (viii)~A bounded regeneration-rate window; annual review is stable on the stage-structured fisheries map (and unstable for the slow-stock Candidate~A hold map); a prospective review-interval test for fast-maturing stocks under $T_r\in[3,12]$~yr.

\section{Why compensatory scalars fail}
\label{sec:why-frameworks-fail}

Scalar aggregation underlies Earth Overshoot Day \cite{lin2018,wackernagel2019,blomqvist2013}, the systems-dynamics overshoot models \cite{meadows1972}, and the communication indices derived from planetary boundaries \cite{rockstrom2009,steffen2015,richardson2023}. Three failure modes are fatal.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Dimensional collapse.} Aggregating incommensurable services destroys the information needed to detect component-specific collapse.
\item \textbf{Flow-only blindness.} A scalar consumption--regeneration comparison cannot detect regeneration maintained by mining non-renewable stocks.
\item \textbf{Compensatory concealment.} A positive aggregate is compatible with an arbitrarily deep deficit in any single component.
\end{enumerate}

The third is not a qualitative risk. It is an identity.

\begin{proposition}[No scalar weighting certifies componentwise sustainability]
\label{prop:no-scalar}
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\mathbf b=(b_1,\dots,b_n)\in\mathbb R^n$ be a service-component balance, $b_i>0$ surplus and $b_i<0$ deficit. Fix any $\mathbf w\in\mathbb R^n_{>0}$ and set $\sigma(\mathbf b)=\mathbf w^\top\mathbf b$. Then for every index $k$ and every $M>0$ there exist $\mathbf b,\mathbf b'$ such that
\begin{equation}
b_k\le -M\quad\text{and}\quad\sigma(\mathbf b)>0,
\qquad
b_k'\ge M\quad\text{and}\quad\sigma(\mathbf b')<0.
\end{equation}
Hence no threshold on $\mathbf w^\top\mathbf b$ certifies $\mathbf b\in\mathbb R^n_+$. Equivalently, no positive linear functional certifies the positive cone. By contrast $\min_i b_i\ge 0$ if and only if $\mathbf b\in\mathbb R^n_+$, and $\|[-\mathbf b]_+\|=\operatorname{dist}(\mathbf b,\mathbb R^n_+)=0$ if and only if $\mathbf b\in\mathbb R^n_+$. For $n\ge 2$ no linear half-space $\{\mathbf b:\mathbf w^\top\mathbf b\ge c\}$ equals the positive orthant. The construction uses an unbounded balance set; on a bounded admissible set a conservative scalar threshold can give one-sided safety, but still cannot identify which component fails. The novelty is the use of this elementary obstruction to design a mass-conserved dynamic architecture, not the geometry itself.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write $\sigma(\mathbf b)=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i b_i$ with $w_i>0$ and $n\ge 2$. Fix an index $k$ and a number $M>0$, and choose $j\neq k$. Define $\mathbf b\in\mathbb R^n$ by $b_k=-M$, $b_j=(w_k M+1)/w_j$, and $b_i=0$ for $i\notin\{k,j\}$. Then
\[
\sigma(\mathbf b)=w_k(-M)+w_j\cdot\frac{w_k M+1}{w_j}=-w_k M+w_k M+1=1>0,
\]
while $b_k=-M$ is arbitrarily negative. For a surplus at component $k$ compatible with an arbitrarily negative aggregate, replace $(b_k,b_j)$ by $(M,-(w_k M+1)/w_j)$. Neither construction uses any special property of $\mathbf w$ beyond positivity, nor any bound on $M$.
\end{proof}

For the bounded sets on which the indices under critique actually operate (e.g., the finite biocapacity aggregates behind Earth Overshoot Day), the relevant reading is the proposition's own bounded-set caveat: a conservative scalar threshold can exclude the most extreme single-component deficits, but it still cannot certify which component, if any, is failing --- the certification failure is generic, not an artefact of unboundedness.

A computational stress test over randomised weights, dimensions $n\in\{2,\dots,8\}$, and thresholds up to $M=10^{12}$ (exact rational arithmetic) confirms both directions. The result is specific to \emph{compensatory linear} aggregation. Non-compensatory scalars --- the minimum margin $\min_i b_i$, the violation magnitude $\|[-\mathbf b]_+\|$, the distance to the positive cone --- do certify componentwise non-negativity, precisely because they forbid offsetting. The diagnostics of this paper are the component-resolved form of those certificates: they retain \emph{which} component fails.

Vector accounting itself is not new. SEEA \cite{seea2014}, integrated reporting \cite{iirc2013}, comprehensive wealth \cite{cwon2021,dasgupta2021}, environmentally extended input--output analysis \cite{leontief1970}, life-cycle assessment \cite{iso14040}, and economy-wide material-flow accounting \cite{eurostat2001,hoekstra2002} already track parallel balances. The analysis combines (i)~a closed, donor-limited flux ledger from which conservation is derived, (ii)~non-compensatory componentwise certification, and (iii)~a delayed institutional layer whose bifurcations are computed exactly and are therefore falsifiable.

Three claims must be kept separate: \emph{empirical degradation} (the record below), \emph{model-defined overshoot} (the framework's own deficit, which these data support qualitatively but do not compute), and \emph{committed collapse} (irreversible loss), which neither the data nor the model establish for the systems listed. The empirical record is already multi-component: six of nine planetary boundaries transgressed \cite{richardson2023}; atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_2$ above the Holocene range \cite{ipcc2021}; grain Zn/Fe density down $20$--$33\%$ from breeding dilution \cite{fan2008,debnath2023} with a further $\mathrm{CO}_2$-driven reduction on top \cite{myers2014}; groundwater extraction exceeding recharge by an order of magnitude in major basins \cite{famiglietti2014,rodell2018}; soil erosion $10$--$100\times$ formation under conventional tillage \cite{montgomery2007}. These are the pattern the vector deficit is built to measure.

\section{The accounting core}
\label{sec:accounting}

Ecological variables are measured in native physical units; economic variables in monetary or index units; prices are exchange rates. Several symbols are deliberately reused with different meanings in different layers; Appendix~\ref{app:params} (Table~\ref{tab:symbols}) tabulates every such reuse, and readers are advised to consult it before reading further. Within one resource system the mass compartments $N,P,W,I,U,A^{\mathrm{act}},A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ are expressed in a single conserved elemental unit, so that the ledger additions below are dimensionally homogeneous. Vector $\min$, $\max$, and the positive part $[\cdot]_+$ are componentwise. For each resource system $i=1,\dots,n$ the state comprises a natural-capital vector $\mathbf N_i$, a service (sustainable-yield) vector $\mathbf S_i$, a demand vector $\mathbf D_i$, an economic product stock $\mathbf P_i$, waste $\mathbf W_j$, an inert sink $\mathbf I_j$, a detritus vector $\mathbf U_i$, an active abiotic pool $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i$, and a geological reservoir $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i$, together with the macroeconomic scalars $K,L,A_{\mathrm{TFP}},Q,T$ and the price vector $\mathbf p_i$.

\subsection{Two abiotic compartments}
\label{sec:abiotic}

A single abiotic reservoir cannot be simultaneously dynamically responsive (so that recovered mass affects regeneration) and effectively infinite (so that logistic growth is recovered as a constitutive limit). The \textbf{active pool} $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i$ is finite and comparable in scale to $\mathbf N_i$: soil solution, mixed layer, shallow groundwater, atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_2$. It supplies regeneration and receives technological recovery. The \textbf{geological reservoir} $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i$ is $10^2$--$10^4$ times larger on policy timescales: bedrock, deep aquifers, the deep ocean. It recharges the active pool and is the source of direct mining (fossil groundwater, phosphate rock).

Net regeneration $\mathbf R_i$ vanishes at carrying capacity. A mature forest still draws continuously on nutrients and water. Gross abiotic uptake is therefore
\begin{equation}
\mathbf B_i(\mathbf N_i,\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i,\mathbf W)
= \mathbf R_i + \boldsymbol\kappa_{A,i}\odot\mathbf N_i\odot\frac{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i}{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i+\mathbf A_{0,i}},
\end{equation}
so $\mathbf B_i>0$ whenever $\boldsymbol\kappa_{A,i},\mathbf N_i>0$. The form does not guarantee $\mathbf B_i\ge\mathbf 0$ when $\mathbf R_i<\mathbf 0$ (stock above carrying capacity); $\mathbf B_i$ remains positive in the parameter regime used here provided $\kappa_{A,i}N_i\ge|R_i|$, but a primitive-flux formulation separating assimilation from mortality would make the sign guaranteed by construction. Both terms of $\mathbf B_i$ are donor-limited and vanish as $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i\to\mathbf 0^+$.

One-way recharge from $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i$ is not a restoring force: $\partial R/\partial A^{\mathrm{act}}$ vanishes as $N\to K$, and the implied recovery time diverges exactly in the mature-stock regime the productivity illusion occupies. Bidirectional exchange is two donor-limited primitive fluxes. The target law is implemented by saturating recharge,
\begin{equation}
\mathbf e_{GA,i}
=
\boldsymbol\omega_{A,i}\odot[\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act,eq}}_i]_+
\odot
\frac{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i}{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i+\mathbf A_{g0,i}},
\qquad
\mathbf e_{AG,i}=\boldsymbol\omega_{A,i}\odot\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i,
\label{eq:exchange-primitive}
\end{equation}
Write $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=A^{\mathrm{geo}}/(A^{\mathrm{geo}}+A_{g0})$. Then $e_{GA}=0$ at $A^{\mathrm{geo}}=0$, and the ideal net $\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)$ is recovered only as $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}\to 1$. The recharge uses $[A^{\mathrm{eq}}]_+$ so that a transiently negative derived target cannot reverse a donor-limited flux. The reduced cores used for bifurcation theorems are stated in the large-reservoir limit $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=1$. For finite $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ the vector field is perturbed by $O(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$, and under the dynamic derived target $U$ feeds back through $\gamma_U U(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$. Mining is donor-limited in the same way extraction is.
\paragraph{Remark ($\mathbf A_{g0}>0$ assumed).} We assume $\mathbf A_{g0,i}>0$ throughout, so $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i/(\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i+\mathbf A_{g0,i})$ is a smooth, strictly decreasing function of the donor level and the recharge varies continuously with $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i$. If any component of $\mathbf A_{g0}=0$, then $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}\equiv 1$ for every $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i>0$, i.e.~recharge is constant until a hard shutoff at $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i=0$ -- a discontinuous perturbation, not a slow donor decline. The $\mathbf A_{g0}=0$ limit is the discontinuous-perturbation corner, not the slow regular donor limit actually used in the paper; the companion never fixed $\mathbf A_{g0}$, the present paper fixes $\mathbf A_{g0}>0$ throughout.

\begin{equation}
\mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i(t)=\mathbf C^A_i(t)\odot\frac{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i}{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i+\mathbf A_{g0,i}}.
\label{eq:mining-limited}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i}{dt}
= -\mathbf B_i + \mathbf e_{GA,i}-\mathbf e_{AG,i}
+ \boldsymbol\gamma_{U,i}\odot\mathbf U_i
+ \sum_j\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{rec}}_{i,j}\bigl(\boldsymbol\rho_{i,j}(T)\odot\mathbf W_j\bigr),
\label{eq:abiotic}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i}{dt}
= -\mathbf e_{GA,i}+\mathbf e_{AG,i} - \mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i(t).
\label{eq:abiotic-geo}
\end{equation}
When $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i$ is frozen, $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act,eq,geo}}_i$ is a constant and \eqref{eq:abiotic} reduces to the previous net-exchange form. The exchange rate $\boldsymbol\omega_{A,i}$ still bounds the active-pool recovery time: $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{rec,act}}_{i,c}\le 1/\omega_{A,i,c}$ uniformly in $N$. At $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i=\mathbf 0$, $\mathbf B_i=\mathbf e_{AG,i}=\mathbf 0$, so $\dot{\mathbf A}^{\mathrm{act}}_i\ge\mathbf 0$. At $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i=\mathbf 0$, $\mathbf e_{GA,i}=\mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i=\mathbf 0$, so $\dot{\mathbf A}^{\mathrm{geo}}_i=\mathbf e_{AG,i}\ge\mathbf 0$. Both orthants are forward invariant (Theorem~\ref{thm:nonneg}).

Write $\mathbf D^{\mathrm{ret}}_i:=\boldsymbol\gamma_{U,i}\odot\mathbf U_i$ for the detrital return flux into the active pool. The geochemical target is derived, not independently specified,
\begin{equation}
\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act,eq}}_i
:= \mathbf A^{\mathrm{act,eq,intrinsic}}_i + \bigl(\boldsymbol\kappa_{A,i}\odot\mathbf K_i - \mathbf D^{\mathrm{ret}}_i\bigr)/\boldsymbol\omega_{A,i},
\label{eq:aeq-derived}
\end{equation}
Two closures of this formula are used below, and they are not interchangeable.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Dynamic derived target.} $\mathbf D^{\mathrm{ret}}_i=\boldsymbol\gamma_{U,i}\odot\mathbf U_i$ tracks the live return. In the ideal large-reservoir limit $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=1$, $\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq}}-A)+\gamma_U U=\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}-A)+\kappa_A K$ identically and
\[
\dot A=-B+\omega_A\bigl(A^{\mathrm{eq,W}}-A\bigr),\qquad A^{\mathrm{eq,W}}=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}+\kappa_A K/\omega_A.
\]
This is the working-core $A$-equation (Theorem~\ref{thm:working-proj}). For $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}<1$ the identity fails by $O(1-\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}})$ and $U$ re-enters $\dot A$.
\item \emph{Fixed intrinsic target.} $A^{\mathrm{eq}}=A^{\mathrm{eq,intrinsic}}$ is held constant (the carrying-capacity calibration, not a live function of $U$). After slaving $U$, one obtains the QSS core of Theorem~\ref{thm:detritus}.
\end{enumerate}
If the detritus compartment is omitted outright, $D^{\mathrm{ret}}=0$ and closure~1 is used with $U$ absent.

Natural turnover is routed to detritus, not to anthropogenic waste:
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\mathbf U_i}{dt}
= \boldsymbol\kappa_{A,i}\odot\mathbf N_i\odot\frac{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i}{\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i+\mathbf A_{0,i}}
- \boldsymbol\gamma_{U,i}\odot\mathbf U_i.
\label{eq:detritus}
\end{equation}
Decomposition $\boldsymbol\gamma_{U,i}\odot\mathbf U_i$ returns to $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i$ independently of recovery technology $T$. The pre-industrial limit $\boldsymbol\rho_{i,j}=\mathbf 0$ therefore closes.

Direct mining drains $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i$ only through the limited flow $\mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i$, which is routed into $\mathbf P_i$ and $\mathbf W_j$ by the same immediate-waste split $\boldsymbol\alpha_i$ used for biological extraction. Any sustained $\mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i>0$ is full geological liquidation on this model's horizon. The unlimited $C^A$ is a capacity, not a flux.

Mining does not enter the specialised deficit. Institutional memory is driven by $qEN-R(N,A^{\mathrm{act}})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:deficit-identity}), never by $C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}$. While recharge holds $A^{\mathrm{act}}\gg A_0$, regeneration stays near logistic, $Z^*=\delta$, and $E=E^*$ as $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ declines. The institutional observer records no deficit. When $A^{\mathrm{geo}}\to 0$, $e_{GA}=C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}=0$, $A^{\mathrm{act}}$ decays on the $\omega_A$ clock, $R$ falls, and the delayed effort law sees a spike set by $\tau_m$ and $\tau$. That is the within-system productivity illusion in the specialised variables. The working-core thresholds $\tau_\pm$ are computed with $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ frozen or omitted.

\subsection{Extraction, liquidation, and the stock equation}

Effort $\mathbf E_i(t)\in[\mathbf 0,\mathbf E_{\max,i}]$ acts on standing stock,
\begin{equation}
\mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{effort}}(t)=q\,\mathbf E_i(t)\odot\mathbf N_i(t).
\end{equation}
This is the sole extraction term in the institutional-failure regime. Because it is proportional to $\mathbf N_i$, it vanishes at the origin for every effort trajectory. The stock equation is
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\mathbf N_i}{dt}
= \mathbf R_i(\mathbf N_i,\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i,\mathbf W)
- \mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{effort}}
- \mathbf N_i\odot\sum_j\boldsymbol\mu_{i,j}\mathbf W_j
+ \boldsymbol\nu_i\odot\mathbf P_i.
\label{eq:nvec}
\end{equation}
Capital liquidation is a diagnostic split of that single flow against the service yield,
\begin{equation}
\bar{\mathbf C}_i=\min\bigl(\mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{effort}},\,\mathbf M_i^\top\mathbf S_i\bigr),\qquad
\boldsymbol\Lambda_i=\max\bigl(\mathbf 0,\,\mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{effort}}-\mathbf M_i^\top\mathbf S_i\bigr),
\label{eq:liquidation-general}
\end{equation}
not a second dynamical term. Here $\mathbf S_i$ is the Liebig service of Section~\ref{sec:structural-production}, which is not in general equal to the regeneration $\mathbf R_i$. A two-term formulation with an unbarriered liquidation top-up drives $N$ through zero in finite time; the single-flow law precludes that.

Recovered waste is routed to $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i$, not to living biomass. Routing recovery to $\mathbf N_i$ would synthesise standing stock from dispersed waste and bypass the abiotic bottleneck the two-pool architecture exists to track.

\subsection{Mass conservation}

Mass-conserved components (physical stocks of one material, within one resource system) are partitioned from functional states (abundance indices, $Z,E,K,L,A_{\mathrm{TFP}},T,\mathbf p,Q$). Conversion tensors satisfy unit-sum constraints in the direction of the flow they route:
\begin{equation}
\sum_i\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{rec}}_{i,j}=\mathbf I_{m_j},\qquad
\sum_j\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{decay}}_{i,j}=\mathbf I_{m_i},\qquad
\sum_j\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{damage}}_{j,i}=\mathbf I_{m_i},\qquad
\sum_j\boldsymbol\varepsilon_{i,j}=\mathbf I_{m_i}.
\end{equation}
Every outflow in the flux ledger (Table~\ref{tab:ledger}) is matched by an inflow of identical magnitude. Differentiating
\begin{equation}
M_{\mathrm{tot}}
= \sum_i\mathbf 1^\top\bigl(\mathbf N_i^{\mathrm{mass}}+\mathbf P_i+\mathbf A^{\mathrm{act}}_i+\mathbf A^{\mathrm{geo}}_i+\mathbf U_i\bigr)
+ \sum_j\mathbf 1^\top(\mathbf W_j+\mathbf I_j)
\end{equation}
and substituting the ledger therefore yields
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\;dM_{\mathrm{tot}}/dt=0\;}\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad M_{\mathrm{tot}}(t)=M_{\mathrm{tot}}(0)\quad\forall t\ge 0.
\label{eq:invariant}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Stoichiometric conservation of the full ledger]
\label{thm:mass-conservation}
Let $X=(N,P,W,I,U,A^{\mathrm{act}},A^{\mathrm{geo}})$ be the mass compartments of one resource system and $\mathcal I$ the incidence matrix of Table~\ref{tab:ledger}. One-way transfers are nonnegative and donor-limited; net regeneration is the difference of two such primitives and is signed when $N>K$. Under the unit-sum routing constraints and $0\le\alpha\le 1$,
\[
\dot X=\mathcal I F(X),\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\mathbf 1^\top X=0.
\]
Hence \eqref{eq:invariant}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The mass vector is $\mathbf m=(N,A^{\mathrm{act}},A^{\mathrm{geo}},U,P,W,I)$ (componentwise, for each resource). Its derivative is $\dot{\mathbf m}=\mathcal I F$, where $F$ is the vector of primitive fluxes in Table~\ref{tab:ledger} and $\mathcal I$ is the incidence matrix of that table. Every primitive is a transfer between two compartments, or a pair of opposite primitives implementing a two-way exchange: the corresponding column of $\mathcal I$ has entries $+1$ and $-1$ in the receiving and donating rows and zeros elsewhere, or a pair of such columns. Routing tensors $(\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{rec}},\boldsymbol\varepsilon,\boldsymbol\alpha)$ are row-stochastic by construction, so each unit of a split flux still sums to one across destinations. Hence $\mathbf 1^\top\mathcal I=0$ and $\mathbf 1^\top\dot{\mathbf m}=\mathbf 1^\top\mathcal I F=0$. Integrating gives $\mathbf 1^\top\mathbf m(t)=\mathbf 1^\top\mathbf m(0)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Mass reconstruction from reduced cores]
\label{cor:mass-recon}
Under the dynamic-target closure with $U$ retained ($\dot U=T-\gamma_U U$) and $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ reconstructed from $e_{GA}-e_{AG}+C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}$, the combined state satisfies Theorem~\ref{thm:mass-conservation}. The omitted-$U$ working core is an open projection: natural turnover $T$ must be routed to a diagnostic detritus or inert sink, and geological drawdown must be reconstructed from the imposed recharge. Without those diagnostic compartments the reduced $(N,A,Z,E)$ trajectory is not mass-closed. If $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$ is frozen, the mass error is $\int_0^t(e_{GA}-e_{AG}+C^{A,\mathrm{lim}})\,ds$, equal in the $\sigma_{\mathrm{geo}}=1$ limit to $\int_0^t[\omega_A(A^{\mathrm{eq,W}}-A^{\mathrm{act}}(s))+C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}(s)]\,ds$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\small
\caption{Flux ledger for the mass-conserved compartments of one resource system (scalar case). Every outflow is matched by an inflow of identical magnitude.}
\label{tab:ledger}
\begin{tabular}{llp{4.6cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Compartment} & \textbf{Flux} & \textbf{Matches} \\
\midrule
$N$ & $+R$; $-C^{\mathrm{effort}}$; $-N\mu W$; $+\nu P$ & internal; $\to P,W$; $\to W$; $\leftarrow P$ \\
$P$ & $+(1-\alpha)C^{\mathrm{effort}}$, $+(1-\alpha)C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}$; $-\lambda P$; $-\nu P$ & $\leftarrow N,A^{\mathrm{geo}}$; $\to W$; $\to N$ \\
$W$ & $+\varepsilon\alpha C^{\mathrm{effort}}$, $+\varepsilon\alpha C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}$; $+\chi^{\mathrm{decay}}\lambda P$; $+\chi^{\mathrm{damage}}N\mu W$; $-\beta W,-\zeta W$; $-\rho W$ & $\leftarrow N,A^{\mathrm{geo}}$; $\leftarrow P$; $\leftarrow N$; $\to I$; $\to A^{\mathrm{act}}$ \\
$I$ & $+\beta W,+\zeta W$ & $\leftarrow W$ \\
$A^{\mathrm{act}}$ & $-B$; $+e_{GA}-e_{AG}$; $+\chi^{\mathrm{rec}}\rho W$; $+\gamma_U U$ & internal; $\leftrightarrow A^{\mathrm{geo}}$; $\leftarrow W$; $\leftarrow U$ \\

\paragraph{Logistic growth as a constitutive limit.}
The regeneration law $R(N,A^{\mathrm{act}})=rN(1-N/K)\cdot A^{\mathrm{act}}/(A^{\mathrm{act}}+A_0)$ recovers the logistic $rN(1-N/K)$ as $A^{\mathrm{act}}/A_0\to\infty$. That is a constitutive (level) limit: it requires the active pool to be large relative to the saturation constant $A_0$, not relative to $N$ or to $A^{\mathrm{geo}}$. The same limit sends
\[
\frac{\partial R}{\partial A^{\mathrm{act}}}=rN\Bigl(1-\frac NK\Bigr)\frac{A_0}{(A^{\mathrm{act}}+A_0)^2}\to 0,
\]
so the Jacobian restoring force on $A^{\mathrm{act}}$ through $R$ vanishes and the pool's linear recovery rate is $\omega_A$ alone. Near-logistic growth and a fast-equilibrating active pool are therefore mutually exclusive. Choosing $A^{\mathrm{act}}\gg A_0$ yields near-logistic $R$ while leaving $A^{\mathrm{act}}$ a slow donor-limited state: a decline of $A$ toward $A_0$ still binds regeneration, but not on the $N$-timescale. The geological reservoir may be treated as frozen on $10$--$100$~yr horizons; the active pool is slow, not static (Section~\ref{sec:four-state}, Theorem~\ref{thm:frozenA}).

\subsection{Services and the vector deficit}

A stock--service matrix $\mathbf M_i$ ($k_i\times m_i$) converts service demand into stock-space extraction in the rational-optimisation regime: $\mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{demand}}=\mathbf M_i^\top\mathbf D_i$. Service yields obey a smooth Liebig law: each component is a $C^\infty$ soft-minimum of saturated sub-yields, recovering the strict minimum as the sharpness $\rho_{i,c}\to\infty$, and is capped at $S_{i,c}^{\max}$. Spatial heterogeneity enters at leading order by Jensen's inequality. For logistic $S(N)=rN(1-N/K)$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E[S(N)]=S(\bar N)-\frac{r}{K}\,\mathrm{Var}(N)
\end{equation}
exactly. A mean-only observer overestimates regenerative capacity by $(r/K)\mathrm{Var}(N)$. Matter on this manuscript's horizon is largely closed; the planet is energetically open. The economy is an internal sub-network of those cycles, not an exogenous forcing. Institutions observe coarse aggregates, so the projection is enactive: it is the decision environment, not a passive summary. The equations below are that cockpit, not a spatially explicit field theory.

The physical deficit is the diagnostic
\begin{equation}
\boldsymbol\Delta_i^{\mathrm{phys}}(t)=\mathbf C_i(t)-\mathbf M_i^\top\mathbf S_i(t),
\label{eq:deficit-phys}
\end{equation}
with $\mathbf C_i$ the operative extraction law. It does not drive the physical ODEs, and it is not equal to $-\dot{\mathbf N}_i$ unless waste-product feedback vanishes and the service is identified with regeneration. Definition~\ref{def:specialisation} makes that identification: a single component, $\boldsymbol\mu=\boldsymbol\nu=\boldsymbol\rho=\mathbf 0$, and $S=R$. On that class, and only on that class, $\boldsymbol\Lambda=[qEN-R]_+=[-\dot N]_+$. In the reduced core the institutional memory is a shifted, floored softplus of that specialised deficit, so that $Z^*=\delta$ is independent of the numerical sharpness $k$.

\subsection{Product, waste, and the inert sink}
\label{sec:waste-loop}

Durability is a material property of extracted matter, not a property of whether extraction exceeded sustainable yield. The diagnostic split $(\bar{\mathbf C}_i,\boldsymbol\Lambda_i)$ therefore never gates physical routing. The product stock receives the durable fraction of \emph{all} extraction, including direct mining:
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\mathbf P_i}{dt}
= (1-\boldsymbol\alpha_i)\odot\bigl(\mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{effort}}+\mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i\bigr)
- \boldsymbol\lambda_i\odot\mathbf P_i
- \boldsymbol\nu_i\odot\mathbf P_i.
\label{eq:product}
\end{equation}
Waste receives immediate extraction waste, product decay, and waste-damage conversion:
\begin{align}
\frac{d\mathbf W_j}{dt}
&= \sum_i\boldsymbol\varepsilon_{i,j}\bigl(\boldsymbol\alpha_i\odot(\mathbf C_i^{\mathrm{effort}}+\mathbf C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_i)\bigr)
+ \sum_i\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{decay}}_{i,j}(\boldsymbol\lambda_i\odot\mathbf P_i)
\nonumber\\
&\quad + \sum_i\boldsymbol\chi^{\mathrm{damage}}_{j,i}\bigl(\mathbf N_i\odot\boldsymbol\mu_{i,j}\mathbf W_j\bigr)
- \boldsymbol\beta_j(\mathbf N)\odot\mathbf W_j
- \boldsymbol\zeta_j T\odot\mathbf W_j
- \sum_i\boldsymbol\rho_{i,j}(T)\odot\mathbf W_j.
\label{eq:wvec}
\end{align}
The inert reservoir captures the irreversible fraction,
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\mathbf I_j}{dt}=\boldsymbol\beta_j(\mathbf N)\odot\mathbf W_j+\boldsymbol\zeta_j T\odot\mathbf W_j,
\label{eq:ivec}
\end{equation}
distinguishing stock pollutants (CO$_2$, persistent plastics) from dissipating flow pollutants. Non-negativity of $\mathbf N_i$ follows from $q\mathbf E_i\odot\mathbf N_i\to\mathbf 0$ at the origin.

\subsection{Structural production: smooth vector Liebig}
\label{sec:structural-production}

Each service component is a $C^\infty$ soft-minimum of saturated sub-yields,
\[
S_{i,c}=S_{i,c}^{\max}\Biggl[-\frac1{\rho_{i,c}}\ln\Biggl(\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{i,c}}w_{m,i,c}
\exp\Bigl(-\rho_{i,c}\frac{\tilde Y_{m,i,c}}{S_{i,c}^{\max}}\Bigr)\Biggr)\Biggr],
\]
with $\sum_m w_{m,i,c}=1$. As $\rho_{i,c}\to\infty$ this is Liebig's law of the minimum. The softmax weights
\[
\pi_{j,i,c}=\frac{w_{j,i,c}\exp(-\rho_{i,c}\tilde Y_{j,i,c}/S_{i,c}^{\max})}{\sum_m w_{m,i,c}\exp(-\rho_{i,c}\tilde Y_{m,i,c}/S_{i,c}^{\max})}
\]
satisfy $\partial S_{i,c}/\partial\tilde Y_{j,i,c}=\pi_{j,i,c}$. Sub-yields include renewable provision $R_{i,c}=r_{i,c}N_{i,c}(1-N_{i,c}/K_{i,c})$ (with an Allee factor where required \cite{courchamp1999,kramer2009}) and critical-regulation sigmoids. The sharpness $\rho_{i,c}$ does not enter the reduced core ODE; it enters the reduction error of Theorem~\ref{thm:weak-coupling} as $e^{-\rho\Delta_y}$ under a yield gap.

\section{Four-layer dynamics}
\label{sec:layers}

Four layers keep normative conditions from violating conservation.

\paragraph{Layer 1} is the physical ledger of Section~\ref{sec:accounting}.

\paragraph{Layer 2} computes diagnostics.
\begin{definition}[Softplus and shifted floored filter]
\label{def:phi}
For $k>0$,
\[
\operatorname{sp}_k(x)=\frac1k\ln\bigl(1+e^{kx}\bigr),\qquad
\Phi_{k,\delta}(x)=\max\Bigl\{0,\,\operatorname{sp}_k(x)-\tfrac{\ln 2}{k}+\delta\Bigr\}.
\]
Vectors are filtered componentwise. Then $\operatorname{sp}_k(0)=\ln 2/k$, $\operatorname{sp}_k'(0)=1/2$, and $\Phi_{k,\delta}(0)=\delta$. If $\delta>0$ the outer floor is inactive in a neighbourhood of zero. We write $\mathrm{softplus}_k\equiv\operatorname{sp}_k$. If the deficit is left dimensional, $k$ has inverse-deficit units; equivalently the argument may be scaled by $\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}$ first. At the baseline $\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}=1$ matches the deficit unit and $k=10$.
\end{definition} The weights $w_i$ in the macroeconomic loss terms are nonnegative and sum to one; $\|\boldsymbol\Delta_i^{\mathrm{econ}}\|$ is the Euclidean norm (any fixed norm only rescales the $w_i$). The vector memory is the leaky integrator
\[
\dot{\boldsymbol\Delta}_i^{\mathrm{phys}}
=\frac1{\tau_m}\Bigl[\max\Bigl(\mathbf 0,\;\mathrm{softplus}_k(\mathbf C_i-\mathbf M_i^\top\mathbf S_i)-\tfrac{\ln 2}{k}\mathbf 1+\boldsymbol\delta\Bigr)-\boldsymbol\Delta_i^{\mathrm{phys}}\Bigr].
\]
The economic deficit is price-weighted by the saturating transform $\tilde p_{i,c}=p_{i,c}/(p_{i,c}+p_{i,c,0})\in[0,1)$,
\[
\Delta_{i,c}^{\mathrm{econ}}=\tilde p_{i,c}\,\max\bigl(0,\;\mathrm{softplus}_k(D_{i,c}-S_{\mathrm{meas},i,c})-\tfrac{\ln 2}{k}+\delta\bigr).
\]
Raw price diverges as $S_{i,c}\to 0$; the saturating weight preserves order without sending capital, TFP, and technology loss rates to infinity.

\paragraph{Layer 3.} Dimensionless inputs $\hat K=K/K_{\mathrm{ref}}$, $\hat L=L/L_{\mathrm{ref}}$. The service-weighted index
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{agg}}=\Bigl(\sum_{i,c}\omega_{i,c}(S_{i,c}/S_{i,c}^{\mathrm{ref}})^\gamma\Bigr)^{1/\gamma}
\]
has substitution elasticity $\sigma_S=1/(1-\gamma)$. Output is the Cobb--Douglas
\[
Q=A_{\mathrm{TFP}}\,\hat K^\alpha\hat L^\beta\mathcal S_{\mathrm{agg}}^{\delta_S},\qquad\alpha+\beta+\delta_S=1,
\]
the $\rho=1$ (weak-sustainability) member of the nested CES
\[
Q=A_{\mathrm{TFP}}\Bigl[\theta(\hat K^\alpha\hat L^\beta)^{(\rho-1)/\rho}+(1-\theta)\mathcal S_{\mathrm{agg}}^{(\rho-1)/\rho}\Bigr]^{\rho/(\rho-1)},
\]
which becomes strong-sustainability as $\rho\to 0$ (standard identification $\rho=(\sigma-1)/\sigma$, $\sigma$ the elasticity of substitution; $\rho=1$ is Cobb--Douglas with $\sigma=1$). The exponent $\delta_S$ is distinct from the baseline deficit $\delta$. Capital, labour, TFP, and technological reconfiguration obey
\begin{align}
\dot K &= \varsigma Q-\delta_K K-\theta K\sum_i w_i\|\boldsymbol\Delta_i^{\mathrm{econ}}\|/\Delta_{i,\mathrm{ref}},
\label{eq:k-corrected}\\
\dot L &= r_L L\bigl(1-L/L_{\max}(Q)\bigr),\qquad L_{\max}(Q)=\max\bigl(L_{\min},\,L_0(Q/Q_0)^\eta\bigr),
\label{eq:l}\\
\dot A_{\mathrm{TFP}} &= \eta_A A_{\mathrm{TFP}}(1-A_{\mathrm{TFP}}/A_{\max})-\nu A_{\mathrm{TFP}}\sum_i w_i\|\boldsymbol\Delta_i^{\mathrm{econ}}\|/\Delta_{i,\mathrm{ref}},
\label{eq:a-corrected}\\
\dot T &= \bigl[\eta_{T,0}+\eta_{T,1}T\sum_i w_i\|\boldsymbol\Delta_i^{\mathrm{econ}}\|/\Delta_{i,\mathrm{ref}}\bigr](1-T/T_{\max}).
\label{eq:t-corrected}
\end{align}

\paragraph{Layer 4.} Service prices $p_{i,c}=p_{i,c,0}+\pi_{i,c}/(S_{i,c}/S_{i,c}^{\mathrm{ref}})$ diverge under scarcity. CES utility maximisation \cite{arrow1961} subject to $\sum_{i,c}p_{i,c}D_{i,c}=(1-\varsigma)Q$ yields $\mathbf D_i$. Perceived yields follow $\dot{\mathbf S}_{\mathrm{meas},i}=\tau_E^{-1}(\mathbf S_i-\mathbf S_{\mathrm{meas},i})$. The DDE history is a constant pre-industrial equilibrium on $[-\tau,0]$, or a $200$-year forward integration of a small perturbation of that equilibrium when a non-constant history is required.

\subsection{Flux decomposition and the productivity gap}
\label{sec:productivity-gap}

Over $[t_0,t]$,
\[
\mathbf N_i(t)-\mathbf N_i(t_0)=\boldsymbol\Phi_R-\boldsymbol\Phi_E-\boldsymbol\Phi_D+\boldsymbol\Phi_P,
\]
with $\Phi_{E,\kappa}$ the integral of the full extraction flow. Recovery enters $\mathbf N_i$ only through $R_{i,\kappa}$. The componentwise sustainability ratio $\mathcal S_{i,\kappa}=(\Phi_{R,\kappa}+\Phi_{P,\kappa})/(\Phi_{E,\kappa}+\Phi_{D,\kappa})$ exceeds $1$ if and only if component $\kappa$ accumulates. The productivity gap $\mathbf G_i=\mathbf S_{\mathrm{meas},i}-\mathbf S_i$ obeys $\dot{\mathbf G}_i=-\tau_E^{-1}\mathbf G_i-\dot{\mathbf S}_i$. When $\tau_E$ is large and true services are declining, $\mathbf G_i$ remains positive in some components: the dynamical form of the productivity illusion.

\section{Depletion horizons}
\label{sec:depletion-horizon}
\label{sec:diagnostics}

Scalar Overshoot Day collapses every component onto one calendar date. We replace it with a vector of compartment-specific horizons.

The dynamic horizon of compartment $\bullet\in\{\mathrm{act},\mathrm{geo}\}$ is the first hitting time
\begin{equation}
T^{\mathrm{dep}}_{i,c}=\inf\bigl\{t>0:A^\bullet_{i,c}(t)\le\epsilon_{i,c}A^\bullet_{i,c}(0)\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
Here $A^{\mathrm{act,min}}_{i,c}$ is an ecological or observational floor: in the groundwater table it is the observed 2002--2023 window minimum; in a model run it is a prescribed threshold. The instantaneous diagnostics are the gross and net horizons
\begin{equation}
\mathcal H^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,c}=\frac{A^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,c}-A^{\mathrm{act,min}}_{i,c}}{B_{i,c}},
\qquad
\mathcal H^{\mathrm{act,net}}_{i,c}=\frac{A^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,c}-A^{\mathrm{act,min}}_{i,c}}{\bigl[-\dot A^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,c}\bigr]_+},
\end{equation}
and the geological analogues with denominator $C^{A,\mathrm{lim}}_{i,c}$ (gross) or $[-\dot A^{\mathrm{geo}}_{i,c}]_+$ (net). The gross active horizon answers the productivity-illusion question: is this stock silently drawing on its support? It is $+\infty$ if $B_{i,c}=0$. The net horizon answers the exhaustion question and is $+\infty$ whenever the compartment is stationary or replenishing. The Depletion Stress Index
\begin{equation}
\Sigma^\bullet_{i,c}=\mathcal H^\bullet_{i,c}/\mathcal T^{\mathrm{rec},\bullet}_{i,c}
\end{equation}
compares horizon to recovery time. Geological recovery is $\gg 10^4$~yr, so any sustained mining gives $\Sigma^{\mathrm{geo}}\ll 1$: chronic structural overshoot, whether or not the horizon is sub-annual. A Service-Specific Overshoot Day is reported only for $\mathcal H^\bullet_{i,c}\le 1$~yr.

\subsection{Application to public data}
\label{sec:adh-results}

We compute the diagnostics on G3P v1.12 groundwater storage anomalies (2002--2023) \cite{guentner2024}, USGS phosphate-rock reserves and production \cite{usgsmcs}, and RAM Legacy v4.66 stock assessments \cite{ricard2012}. No dynamical parameter of the reduced core is fitted. None of the reported numbers is a computed instance of the model's own first-hitting time $T^{\mathrm{dep}}$: the groundwater column is a trend-to-window-minimum extrapolation, the phosphate column a reserve-life ratio, and the fisheries column a pure-decay proxy with recruitment omitted (its caption states it is not an abiotic horizon). They are descriptive, component-resolved diagnostics in the framework's two-pool logic, not dynamical predictions of the reduced core.
